title: 情報理論
subtitle: Information Theory
educationalGoal: Considerable progress has been made in computer networks and ever-increasing amounts of information are now being exchanged. In this course, we learn the information theory developed by Shannon. First, we learn how to quantify information and related knowledge based on the probability theory. Next, we study the information source and its coding method. Finally, we learn how channel coding can be used to correct errors that have occurred in the channel.
advice: Information theory can be used to quantify and encode information output by an information source. It can also be used to correct errors that have occurred in the channel. The topics of this course are as follows: 1. Set and probability 2. Conditional probability and Bayes' theorem 3. Definition of information content and entropy 4. Information source 5. Entropy of information source 6. Source coding 7. Channel coding and error correction
requiredKnowledge: Students are expected to review the following: (1) expected value and variance taken up in "Statistics for Engineers", (2) how to calculate them, and (3) logarithm calculations. If there is anything they cannot understand, they will need to resolve those issues by utilizing office hours. Students are expected to make good use of the exercises at the back of the textbook.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain terms such as information content, entropy, information source, and coding.
Be able to explain the source coding theorem.
Be able to perform Shannon-Fano coding.
Be able to perform Huffman coding.
Be able to explain error correcting code by parity check.
